L1@P0: A NOTE ON DIVISORIAL CORRESPONDENCES OF
L2@P0: EXTENSIONS OF ABELIAN SCHEMES BY TORI
L3@P0: CRISTIANA BERTOLIN AND FEDERICA GALLUZZI
L4@P0: Dedicated to M. Raynaud
L5@P0: Abstract. Let S be a locally noetherian scheme and consider two extensions G1 and G2
L6@P0: of abelian S-schemes by S-tori. In this note we prove that the f ppf-sheaf CorrS(G1, G2) of
L7@P0: divisorial correspondences between G1 and G2 is representable. Moreover, using divisorial
L8@P0: correspondences, we show that line bundles on an extension G of an abelian scheme by a
L9@P0: torus define group homomorphisms between G and PicG/S.

L18@P0: case: divisorial correspondences between group schemes which are extensions of an abelian

L73@P1: 1. Representability of Corr
L74@P1: In [6, Thm 1] Murre gives a criterion for a contravariant functor from the category of
L75@P1: schemes over S to the category of sets to be representable by an unramified, separated
L76@P1: S-scheme which is locally of finite type over S. Using this criterion, he proves the representability of the f ppf-sheaf CorrS(X1, X2) with X1 and X2 proper and flat S-schemes (see
L77@P1: [6, Thm 4]). We adapt his results to extensions of abelian schemes by tori which are not
L78@P1: proper.
L79@P1: Theorem 1.1. Consider two extensions p1 : G1 → S, p2 : G2 → S of abelian schemes by tori.
L80@P1: Suppose that the structural morphisms pi satisfy pi∗OGi = OS universally for i = 1, 2. The
L81@P1: f ppf-sheaf CorrS(G1, G2) of divisorial correspondences between G1 and G2 is representable
L82@P1: by an S-group scheme, locally of finite presentation, separated and unramified over S.
L83@P1: Proof. We have to prove that the functor CorrS(G1, G2) verifies the properties (F1), ...,(F8)

L85@P1: follow from the same properties of PicG1×SG2/S. Concerning property (F3), by [7, Prop II
L86@P1: 2.4 (2) (i)] the extension Gi (for i = 1, 2) is S-pure and therefore [8, Chp 37, Lem 27.6 (2),
L87@P1: Def 21.1] implies that there exists a universal flattening of Gi, that is the flattening functor
L88@P1: is representable. Now using [6, Thm 2], (F3) follows from the same property of PicG1×SG2/S.

L22: 【8†Proposition 99.11.8.】 Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to B$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume that
L23: 
L24:   1. $f$ is flat, of finite presentation, and proper, and
L25: 
L26:   2. $\mathcal{O}_ T \to f_{T, *}\mathcal{O}_{X_ T}$ is an isomorphism for all schemes $T$ over $B$.
L27: 
L28: Then $\mathrm{Pic}_{X/B}$ is an algebraic space.
L29: Proof. There exists a surjective, flat, finitely presented morphism $B' \to B$ of algebraic spaces such that the base change $X' = X \times _ B B'$ over $B'$ has a section: namely, we can take $B' = X$. Observe that $\mathrm{Pic}_{X'/B'} = B' \times _ B \mathrm{Pic}_{X/B}$. Hence $\mathrm{Pic}_{X'/B'} \to \mathrm{Pic}_{X/B}$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat, and finitely presented.
L30: Hence, if we can show that $\mathrm{Pic}_{X'/B'}$ is an algebraic space, then it follows that $\mathrm{Pic}_{X/B}$ is an algebraic space by Bootstrap, Theorem 【14†80.10.1】. In this way we reduce to the case described in the next paragraph.
L31: In addition to the assumptions of the proposition, assume that we have a section $\sigma : B \to X$. By Proposition 【15†99.10.2】 we see that $\mathcal{P}\! \mathit{ic}_{X/B}$ is an algebraic stack. By Lemma 【16†99.11.6】 and Algebraic Stacks, Lemma 【17†94.15.4】 we see that $\mathcal{P}\! \mathit{ic}_{X/B, \sigma }$ is an algebraic stack.
L32: By Lemma 【10†99.11.7】 and Algebraic Stacks, Lemma 【18†94.8.2】 we see that $T \mapsto \mathop{\mathrm{Ker}}(\sigma _ T^* : \mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}\nolimits (X_ T) \to \mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}\nolimits (T))$ is an algebraic space. By Lemma 【19†99.11.4】 this functor is the same as $\mathrm{Pic}_{X/B}$. $\square$
